questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows a beam $AB$ with weight $24\,\mathrm{N}$ and length $6\,\mathrm{m}$.

The beam is suspended by two light vertical ropes. The ropes are attached to the points $C$ and $D$ on the beam where $AC = x$ metres and $CD = 2\,\mathrm{m}$.

The tension in the rope attached to the beam at $C$ is double the tension in the rope attached to the beam at $D$.

The beam is modelled as a uniform rod, resting horizontally in equilibrium.

Find

parts.text:
(i) the tension in the rope attached to the beam at $D$.
(ii) the value of $x$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathrm{M}(A)$: $(2T\times x)+T(x+2)=(24\times 3)$ M1: Forms a moments equation in $x$ and $T$ only with the correct no. of terms. Allow consistent extra $g$'s. M0 if no $x$. A1: Correct unsimplified moments equation. Where two moments equations are used, award this mark for the first correct equation.
Second equation (vert): $3T=24$ M1: Resolves vertically to give equation in $T$ only or a second moments equation in $x$ and $T$ (M0 if no $x$). Must be dimensionally correct with the correct no. of terms.
Alternative moments equations in $x$ and $T$: $\mathrm{M}(C)$: $24(3-x)=T\times 2$; $\mathrm{M}(G)$: $2T(3-x)=T(x-1)$; $\mathrm{M}(D)$: $(2T\times 2)=24\times(x-1)$; $\mathrm{M}(B)$: $2T(6-x)+T(4-x)=(24\times 3)$; $\mathrm{M}(C)$: $\frac{24x}{6}\times\frac{x}{2}+2T=\frac{24(6-x)}{6}\times\frac{(6-x)}{2}$
$T=8$ (N) A1: Correct value for tension at $D$.
$x=\frac{7}{3}$ accept 2.3 or better A1: Correct value for $x$. Accept 2.3 or better.
N.B. If $T$ and $2T$ the wrong way round or they use $24g$, can score max M1A0M1A0A0.

questions.notes: Single part with (i)/(ii) sub-requests but one printed mark bracket (5), so treated as one part with label null.

questions.stem:
Two fixed points, $A$ and $B$, are on a straight horizontal road.

The **acceleration-time** graph in Figure 2 represents the motion of a car travelling along the road as it moves from $A$ to $B$.

At time $t = 0$, the car passes through $A$ with speed $8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

At time $t = 20\,\mathrm{s}$, the car passes through $B$ with speed $v\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
$v=u+at$: $w=8+(-0.5)(4)$ M1 (the value of $w$ may not be seen). Complete method for finding the velocity ($w$) when $t=4$. M0 if $u=0$. N.B. 6 on its own can imply this mark.
$v=u+at$: $v=w+(1.2)(10)$ M1: Method completed to show the speed when $t=20$. M0 if initial speed is not $w$.
$v=18$* A1*: Fully correct solution leading to given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Sketch a speed-time graph for the motion of the car from $A$ to $B$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Correct shape of graph.
B1: Correct time labels 4, 10, 20.
B1: Correct speed labels 6, 8, 18.
N.B. Solid vertical line(s) B0 for the shape.

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
Clear attempt to find distance using the area under their graph from $t=0$ to $t=20$ or another suitable method, even if they are using the wrong shapes. M1: Complete method to find distance travelled in 20 seconds. May use speed-time graph or suvat equations for three sections (28m, 36m, 120m) of the journey. Award this mark for a clear attempt to find the area and penalise errors in the A marks. M0 if graph does not have three sections.
Distance $=\frac{(8+\text{``6''})\times 4}{2}+(6\times\text{``6''})+\frac{(\text{``6''}+18)\times 10}{2}$ OR $=(6\times 4)+\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times(8-6)+(6\times 6)+(6\times 10)+\frac{1}{2}\times 10\times(18-6)$ A1ft: Equation with at most one error, ft their ``6''. A1ft: Correct equation, ft their ``6''.
$=184$ (m) A1: Correct final answer.

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors directed due east and due north respectively.]

A particle $P$ moves with constant acceleration $(-\lambda\mathbf{i} + 2\lambda\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, where $\lambda$ is a positive constant.

At time $t = 0$, the velocity of $P$ is $(5\mathbf{i} - 8\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the velocity of $P$ when $t = 5\,\mathrm{s}$, giving your answer in terms of $\mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{j}$ and $\lambda$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: $(5\mathbf{i}-8\mathbf{j})+5(-\lambda\mathbf{i}+2\lambda\mathbf{j})$ (m s$^{-1}$) isw M1 A1: Use of $v=u+at$ to form a vector expression in $\lambda$ and $t$. M1; Correct unsimplified expression with $t=5$ A1. N.B. Allow use of column vectors for the M mark but not for the A mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The speed of $P$ when $t = 5\,\mathrm{s}$ is $13\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

(b) Show that
$$25\lambda^2 - 42\lambda - 16 = 0$$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$13=\sqrt{(5-5\lambda)^2+(-8+10\lambda)^2}$ M1 A1: Collect $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s and correct use of Pythagoras to form an equation in $\lambda$ M1; Correct equation A1.
$169=25-50\lambda+25\lambda^2+64-160\lambda+100\lambda^2$
$25\lambda^2-42\lambda-16=0$* A1* cso: Expand brackets and correctly reach the GIVEN answer. N.B. Allow $0=25\lambda^2-42\lambda-16$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the direction of motion of $P$ when $t = 4\,\mathrm{s}$, giving your answer as a bearing to the nearest degree.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$(-2\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$ seen or implied B1: Or column vector.
$(5\mathbf{i}-8\mathbf{j})+(-2\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})4$ M1 A1: Complete method to find the velocity when $t=4$ M1; Correct unsimplified expression A1. Note the correct velocity is $v=-3\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j}$
M1: Use their velocity vector at $t=4$ with trig to find a relevant angle. e.g. $\tan^{-1}\left(\pm\frac{8}{3}\right)$, $\tan^{-1}\left(\pm\frac{3}{8}\right)$, $\sin^{-1}\left(\pm\frac{8}{\sqrt{73}}\right)$,...
$339°$ A1: Cao. Degrees sign not required. N.B. if they work with both values of $\lambda$, can score max all the marks except the last one.

questions.stem:
Figure 3 shows a small ring of mass $0.2\,\mathrm{kg}$ attached to one end of a light inextensible string.

The ring is **threaded** onto a fixed rough vertical rod.

The string is taut and makes an angle $\theta$ with the rod, as shown in Figure 3, where $\tan\theta = \frac{12}{5}$

Given that the ring is in equilibrium and that the tension in the string is $10\,\mathrm{N}$,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the ring,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$F=10\cos\theta-0.2g$ or $F=0.2g-10\cos\theta$ M1 A1: Resolve vertically, dimensionally correct, condone sin/cos confusion and sign errors M1; Correct unsimplified equation A1.
$|F|=1.9$ or $1.89$ (N) A1: Correct value for Friction, must be positive. N.B. If they use $\mu R$ as their notation for $F$ and never separate $\mu$ and $R$, allow M1A1A1. If, however, they do separate them, give M1A1A0.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) state the direction of the frictional force acting on the ring.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: Friction acts downwards or down. A1: Correct direction from a correct, but possibly unrounded, answer to part (a). A0 for anything else.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The coefficient of friction between the ring and the rod is $\frac{1}{4}$

Given that the ring is in equilibrium, and that the tension in the string, $T$ newtons, can now vary,

(c) (i) find the minimum value of $T$
(ii) find the maximum value of $T$
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
$R=T\sin\theta$ (i.e. $R=\frac{12T}{13}$) M1 A1: Resolve perpendicular to the rod. Must be dimensionally correct and have correct no of terms. Condone sin/cos confusion. N.B. M0 if they use $T=10$. A1: Correct unsimplified equation.
$F=\frac{1}{4}R$ B1: seen or implied.
Resolve vertically M1: Resolve parallel to the rod for either case. Must be dimensionally correct and have correct no of terms. Condone sin/cos confusion. N.B. M0 if they use $T=10$ or if they use $F$ from part (a).
For min value $T\cos\theta=0.2g-F$ A1: Correct minimum case equation.
For max value $T\cos\theta=0.2g+F$ A1: Correct maximum case equation.
(i) Min $T$: $3.2$ or $3.19$ (N) A1: cao for min $T$. Allow $0.325g$
(ii) Max $T$: $13$ or $12.7$ (N) A1: cao for max $T$. Allow $1.3g$
N.B. Penalise over accuracy once for the whole question and penalise the FIRST time it is seen. N.B. If 2 instead of 0.2 is used throughout the WHOLE question, treat as a MR. N.B. If only one found and no labels, allow the A mark for the equation but must state which one it is to score the A mark for the answer. N.B. If both correctly found and no labels, allow all the marks. N.B. If both correctly found but the answers are labelled wrongly, lose the final two A marks.

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors directed due east and due north respectively and position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin $O$.]

At 12:00, a ship $P$ sets sail from a harbour with position vector $(15\mathbf{i} + 36\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km}$.
At 12:30, $P$ is at the point with position vector $(20\mathbf{i} + 34\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km}$.

Given that $P$ moves with constant velocity,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that the velocity of $P$ is $(10\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\frac{(20\mathbf{i}+34\mathbf{j})-(15\mathbf{i}+36\mathbf{j})}{0.5}$ oe M1: Complete method to find an expression for the velocity. Allow if they use 30 minutes. Give M1A0, if there are missing brackets.
$(10\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})$* A1*: Reaches the given answer from fully correct working.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- N.B. Allow use of column vectors throughout apart from the A marks in (a) and (b).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At time $t$ hours after 12:00, the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}\,\mathrm{km}$.

(b) Find an expression for $\mathbf{p}$ in terms of $\mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{j}$ and $t$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: $(15\mathbf{i}+36\mathbf{j})+t(10\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})$ M1 A1: Finds an expression for $\mathbf{p}$ in terms of $t$ with the correct structure M1; Correct answer in terms of $\mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{j}$ and $t$ A1.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A second ship $Q$ is also travelling at a constant velocity.

At time $t$ hours after 12:00, the position vector of $Q$ is given by $\mathbf{q}\,\mathrm{km}$, where

$$\mathbf{q} = (42 - 8t)\mathbf{i} + (9 + 14t)\mathbf{j}$$

Ships $P$ and $Q$ are modelled as particles.

If both ships maintained their course,

(c) (i) verify that they would collide at 13:30
(ii) find the position vector of the point at which the collision would occur.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Verify using $t=1.5$ in $\mathbf{p}$ or $\mathbf{q}$ M1: Substitutes $t=1.5$ into the given $\mathbf{q}$ or their $\mathbf{p}$.
$\mathbf{p}=(15\mathbf{i}+36\mathbf{j})+1.5(10\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})=30\mathbf{i}+30\mathbf{j}$ A1: P equation correct.
$\mathbf{q}=(42-8\times 1.5)\mathbf{i}+(9+14\times 1.5)\mathbf{j}=30\mathbf{i}+30\mathbf{j}$ A1: Q equation correct. N.B. $\mathbf{p}$ or $\mathbf{q}=30\mathbf{i}+30\mathbf{j}$ alone can imply a correct equation in each case.
(ii) $30\mathbf{i}+30\mathbf{j}$ A1 (B1). N.B. The A mark for (ii) is now to be treated as a B mark.
ALT1 (i) M1: Equates coefficients of $\mathbf{i}$ or $\mathbf{j}$ using the given $\mathbf{q}$ and their $\mathbf{p}$. Equate $\mathbf{i}$'s: $15+10t=42-8t \to t=1.5$ A1; $\mathbf{j}$'s: $36-4t=9+14t \to t=1.5$ A1. N.B. Allow both A marks if they only write $t=1.5$ once. (ii) $30\mathbf{i}+30\mathbf{j}$ A1(B1) seen.
ALT2 (i) M1: Uses ratio: $\frac{15+10t}{36-4t}=\frac{42-8t}{9+14t}$; $\to t=1.5$ or $-8.5$ A1; verifies that components are both 30 at $t=1.5$ A1. (ii) $30\mathbf{i}+30\mathbf{j}$ A1(B1) seen.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
At 12:30 $Q$ changes speed and direction to avoid the collision.

Ship $Q$ now travels due north with a constant speed of $15\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$

Ship $P$ maintains the same constant velocity throughout.

(d) Find the exact distance between $P$ and $Q$ at 14:30
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
Position of $P$ at 14:30 $=40\mathbf{i}+26\mathbf{j}$ B1: Position of $P$ at 14:30.
Position of $Q$ when $t=0.5$: $\mathbf{q}=(42-8\times 0.5)\mathbf{i}+(9+14\times 0.5)\mathbf{j}$ $(=38\mathbf{i}+16\mathbf{j})$ M1: Use $t=0.5$ to find the new position of $Q$ at 12:30.
$15\mathbf{j}$ seen or implied B1: Correct expression seen for new velocity of $Q$.
New position of $Q$ at time 14:30 $\mathbf{q}=(38\mathbf{i}+16\mathbf{j})+2(15\mathbf{j})$ M1: Complete method to find the new position of $Q$ at 14:30, using their new $v$ for $Q$. N.B. M0 if 2.5 is used.
$\mathbf{q}=38\mathbf{i}+46\mathbf{j}$ A1: Correct position.
$|PQ|=\sqrt{(40-38)^2+(26-46)^2}$ dM1: Use of Pythagoras to find the distance. Dependent on both previous M marks.
$=\sqrt{404}$ or $2\sqrt{101}$ (km) A1: Correct surd answer.

questions.stem:
Figure 4 shows a block $A$ of mass $m$ held at rest on a rough plane.
The plane is inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal and the coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is $\mu$.

One end of a light inextensible string is now attached to $A$. The string passes over a small smooth pulley which is fixed at the top of the plane.
The other end of the string is attached to a block $B$ of mass $km$.
Block $B$ hangs vertically below the pulley, with the string taut.

The string from $A$ to the pulley lies along a line of greatest slope of the plane.

Both $A$ and $B$ are modelled as particles.

When the system is released from rest, $A$ moves up the plane and the tension in the string is $\frac{4mg}{3}$

Given that $\mu = \frac{1}{3}$ and $\tan\alpha = \frac{7}{24}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) (i) find the magnitude of the acceleration of $A$, giving your answer in terms of $g$,
(ii) find the value of $k$.
(9)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) For $A$: $\frac{4mg}{3}-mg\sin\alpha-F=ma$ M1 A1: For $A$ use $F=ma$ parallel to the plane. Must be dimensionally correct and have correct no of terms. Condone sin/cos confusion. N.B. If they use $T$ in this equation and never replace it, allow M1. A1: Correct unsimplified equation. N.B. $a$ could be replaced by $-a$.
$R=mg\cos\alpha$ M1 A1: Resolve perpendicular to the plane. Must be dimensionally correct and have correct no of terms. Condone sin/cos confusion. A1: Correct equation.
Use of $F=\frac{1}{3}R$ in an equation. M1: Use of $F=\frac{1}{3}R$.
$a=\frac{11g}{15}$ or $0.73g$ or better A1: Correct answer.
(ii) For $B$: $kmg-\frac{4mg}{3}=kma$ M1 A1: For $B$ use $F=ma$ vertically. Must be dimensionally correct and have correct no of terms. Condone sin/cos confusion. N.B. Must have $km$ on both sides for this mark. N.B. If they use $T$ in this equation and never replace it, allow M1. A1: Correct unsimplified equation. N.B. $a$ could be replaced by $-a$, but must be consistent with the equation for $A$.
$k=5$ A1: correct answer.
N.B. Either equation of motion could be replaced by a whole system equation: $kmg-mg\sin\alpha-F=(k+1)ma$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the magnitude of the resultant force exerted on the pulley by the string, giving your answer in terms of $m$ and $g$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Complete method to find resultant force $2T\cos\left(\frac{90°-\alpha}{2}\right)$ M1 A1: allow sin/cos confusion.
Substitute $T=\frac{4mg}{3}$ and trig dM1.
$\frac{32mg}{15}$ or $2.1mg$ or better A1: Correct answer.
ALT1: Use of cosine rule: $\sqrt{T^2+T^2-2(T)(T)\cos(90+\alpha)}$ M1 A1; Substitute $T=\frac{4mg}{3}$ and trig dM1; Correct answer. Allow $\sqrt{\frac{1024m^2g^2}{225}}$ or similar A1.
ALT2: Use of vert and horiz components to find the resultant: $\sqrt{(T\cos\alpha)^2+(T+T\sin\alpha)^2}$ M1 A1; Substitute $T=\frac{4mg}{3}$ and trig dM1; Correct answer. Allow $\sqrt{\frac{1024m^2g^2}{225}}$ or similar A1.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- dM1: Substitute $T=\frac{4mg}{3}$ and trig, dependent on previous M mark
- (b) ALT1 M1: Complete method – must involve $\alpha$ or its numerical value
- (b) ALT2 M1: Complete method, allow sin/cos confusion
